The wavelength of yellow light is longer than the wavelength of blue light.

As a result, the separation between maxima in the interference pattern increases.

The refractive index of vacuum is less than the refractive index of water, so distance between maxima increases OR the intensity of the pattern increases.

(Description of single-slit diffraction pattern)

There will be a bright central maximum and secondary maxima.

The width of the central maximum is larger than the width of the secondary maxima.

The intensity of the pattern will be lower than previously.

question.html:
In an underwater experiment, monochromatic blue light is incident on a double-slit. The slits are mm apart and the distance between the central maximum and the first minimum is mm. An interference pattern is observed on a screen at a distance x from the slits.

a. State what is meant by the superposition of waves.

  [1]

b. Explain how minima are formed in the pattern.

  [2]

c. Express the wavelength of the incident light in terms of x.

  [2]

d. Hence find the value of x, given that the frequency of the incident light is THz.

  [2]

e. Outline the changes to the interference pattern when the blue light is replaced by yellow light.

  [2]

f. The experiment is now carried out in vacuum. State and explain one change to the appearance of the interference pattern.

  [2]

g. Describe how the pattern appears on the screen when one of the slits is covered.  

  [2]
